data.name: ConnectionsTitle
data.comment: Title of the Connections screen.

data.name: ConnectionsZwiftCard
data.comment: Screen reader name of the card on the Connections screen that shows the Zwift status.

data.name: ZwiftConnected
data.value: Zwift is connected to Voltage Gamepad
data.comment: Zwift status on the Connections screen when Zwift is connected. Keep Voltage Gamepad, which is the device name Zwift shows for this app.

data.name: ZwiftNotConnected
data.comment: Zwift status on the Connections screen when Zwift is not connected.

data.name: ConnectionsControllerCard
data.comment: Screen reader name of the card on the Connections screen that shows your controller.

data.name: ConnectionsControllerHere
data.comment: Connections screen, your controller card, when a controller is connected. {0} is the controller name, for example Xbox Series X Controller.

data.name: ConnectionsControllerAwake
data.comment: Connections screen, second line under the controller name when a controller is connected.

data.name: ConnectionsNoController
data.comment: Connections screen, your controller card, when no controller is connected. It asks the person to press a button on the controller to wake it.

data.name: ConnectionsLooking
data.comment: Connections screen, second line when no controller is connected. The app is still scanning for one.

data.name: ConnectionsPickerLabel
data.comment: Connections screen, label of the dropdown that switches to another connected controller.

data.name: ConnectionsPairBluetooth
data.comment: Connections screen, button that opens the Windows Bluetooth settings so the person can pair a controller.

data.name: ConnectionsShowMeHow
data.comment: Connections screen, button on the Zwift card that shows the three steps to pair with Zwift again.

data.name: ConnectionsHideSteps
data.comment: Connections screen, button on the Zwift card that hides the three steps to pair with Zwift. It replaces Show me how while the steps are open.

data.name: ConnectionsTrainerReminder
data.value: Set Power Source back to your trainer in Zwift.
data.comment: Connections screen, reminder under the Zwift status while Zwift is connected. Power Source is the Zwift setting that picks the trainer.

data.name: ZwiftStepPowerSource
data.comment: Zwift step 1, with its number. In Zwift, the person sets the Power Source device to Voltage Gamepad. Keep Power Source and Voltage Gamepad as they appear in Zwift.

data.name: ZwiftStepControls
data.comment: Zwift step 2, with its number. In Zwift, the person sets the Controls device to Voltage Gamepad. Keep Controls and Voltage Gamepad as they appear in Zwift.

data.name: ZwiftStepTrainer
data.comment: Zwift step 3, with its number. In Zwift, the person sets the Power Source device back to their trainer. Keep Power Source as it appears in Zwift.

data.name: AppearanceLight
data.comment: Settings, app theme choice.

data.name: AppearanceDark
data.comment: Settings, app theme choice.

data.name: AppearanceMatchWindows
data.comment: Settings, app theme choice that follows the Windows app mode.

data.name: ButtonsTitle
data.comment: Title of the Buttons screen.

data.name: ButtonsControllerName
data.comment: Buttons screen, line under the title that names the controller. {0} is the controller name, for example Xbox Series X Controller.

data.name: ButtonsHint
data.value: Press a button on your controller to select it.
data.comment: Buttons screen hint under the title. Pressing a button on the controller selects that button's row.

data.name: ButtonsNoController
data.comment: Buttons screen when no controller is connected. It asks the person to press a button on the controller to wake it.

data.name: ButtonsLooking
data.comment: Buttons screen, second line when no controller is connected. The app is still scanning for one.

data.name: ButtonsMappingPicker
data.comment: Screen reader name of the dropdown that lists the saved mappings (what each button does) for the controller.

data.name: ButtonsUnsaved
data.comment: Buttons screen, shown next to the selected mapping when it has edits that are not saved.

data.name: ButtonsSave
data.comment: Button on the Buttons screen that saves the changes to the selected mapping.

data.name: ButtonsSaveAs
data.comment: Button on the Buttons screen that saves the current buttons as a new mapping.

data.name: ButtonsDelete
data.comment: Button on the Buttons screen that deletes the selected mapping.

data.name: ButtonsMore
data.value: More: rename, import, open folder, reset to default
data.comment: Screen reader name of the More button next to Save on the Buttons screen.

data.name: ButtonsMenuImport
data.comment: Menu item on the Buttons screen. It opens a file picker to import a mapping.

data.name: ButtonsMenuRename
data.comment: Menu item on the Buttons screen. It renames the selected mapping.

data.name: ButtonsMenuOpenFolder
data.comment: Menu item on the Buttons screen. It opens the folder that holds the saved mappings in File Explorer.

data.name: ButtonsMenuReset
data.comment: Menu item on the Buttons screen. It sets every button to what the Default mapping does.

data.name: ButtonsShowOthers
data.comment: Checkbox on the Buttons screen. When checked, the mapping list also shows mappings saved for other controllers.

data.name: ButtonsShowOthersTip
data.value: Picking one saves a copy for this controller.
data.comment: Tooltip of the checkbox that shows mappings from other controllers.

data.name: ButtonsTabs

data.comment: Tab on the Buttons screen that lists the buttons, the D-pad, and the bumpers.

data.name: ButtonsTabSticks
data.comment: Tab on the Buttons screen that lists the sticks and the triggers.

data.name: ButtonsRowName
data.comment: Screen reader name of a row on the Buttons screen. {0} is the input, for example Right bumper, and {1} is what it does, for example Shift up.

data.name: ButtonsChanged
data.comment: Buttons screen, shown on a row when what that button does differs from the saved mapping.

data.name: ButtonsTriggers

data.name: ButtonsTriggerFill
